Years later, Chen rebuilt parts of his public life outside mainstream Hong Kong entertainment. He focused on fashion, business and creative projects, particularly through his streetwear label CLOT. While he returned to selected film, music and media work, the scandal continued to follow him.

In the CNN interview, Chen appeared reflective rather than defensive. He acknowledged that he could not undo what happened, but said he hoped people would understand the human cost of the scandal — not only for him, but especially for the women whose privacy was violated.

The episode remains one of the most consequential celebrity privacy scandals in Asia, remembered not simply for the leaked images, but for what it revealed about the Internet’s ability to amplify humiliation, damage reputations and permanently alter lives.
